findings.location: crates/foundry-acceptance/tests/features/canzan-theme-system.feature:164-170, the only reading of the migrated law, against ADR-NAV-POLISH-002
findings.obligation: ADR-NAV-POLISH-002 and L7: a rail control drawn as text plus an icon owes its word 4.5:1 instead of a 3:1 boundary, and a control inside .app-shell that draws no visible word keeps the boundary rule.
findings.observation: In the two shipped geometries no row opens, both lower controls draw no word, so the migrated predicate puts them on the wordless side where they measure 0:1. Narrowed to icons: [data-nav-collapsed] .sidebar__label takes clip-path inset(50%) in a 1 px box and [data-nav-collapsed] .theme-toggle__mode takes display none. At phone width: .sidebar__label takes the same clip. There .sidebar__item has border 0 over a transparent fill and .theme-toggle has border 0 over var(--cz-bg-2), the surface the ratio is taken against. The ADR reads 'drawn as text plus an icon' and 'exactly as the rail links are', and does not say which of the two rules holds when the rail draws the icon alone. The scenario opens one geometry only, the open rail at the harness desk viewport, so neither the scope of the law nor the shipped result is observed there.
findings.remediation: Decide in ADR-NAV-POLISH-002 whether the exemption belongs to the rail-control class in every geometry, as 'exactly as the rail links are' suggests, or only where a word is actually drawn. If only where a word is drawn, say what identifies the two narrowed controls instead. The oracle then adds the row for the decided geometry.

findings.obligation: Risk Y8: an exemption that reads the fill, the tag or the class instead of the visible word must stay caught, and the assertion message claims it proves a control drawn as a glyph with no word of its own was read.
findings.observation: The counter increments for every non-exempt control that carries a glyph, whatever word it draws, so a worded control outside the nav satisfies it as well; the message names a case the count does not test. Against the named bypass it is silent: widen the exemption to 'the own fill is transparent' and the shipped glyph-only button.nav-collapse, whose fill is the opaque var(--cz-bg-2), stays non-exempt, stays counted, and the assertion still passes while every quiet control of the shell has left the reading. The sibling half is anchored correctly, on the word Sign out.
findings.remediation: Count only a control that carries a glyph AND draws no word, that is glyph true and word trimmed empty, mirroring the Sign out anchor on the other side. The shipped button.nav-collapse satisfies that tighter count today, so the guard stays non-vacuous.

findings.location: crates/foundry-acceptance/tests/features/canzan-theme-system.feature:169, the step 'a nav control that draws its own word beside its glyph has that word legible at 4.5 to 1 instead'
findings.obligation: A row states what the reading observes, in the operator's words: assert the promised observation and nothing the reading cannot see.
findings.observation: At the desk width this scenario reads, .sidebar__icon is display none, so the sign-out submit - the control the reading anchors on - draws its word alone and no glyph beside it. The exemption's glyph term is a document-presence fact, any svg or [aria-hidden=true] descendant, which the probe comment states plainly and the row's words deny; it is also near vacuous for the shell, because every nav control holds such a descendant. The reading therefore turns on the drawn word alone, which is sound, but the row promises a picture the operator does not get in the geometry read.
findings.remediation: Word the row for what is read - a nav control the operator finds by its own visible word - or read the glyph as drawn, and then say that the open rail draws none.

findings.location: crates/foundry-acceptance/src/steps/feature_canzan_theme.rs, assert_the_word_is_legible, the two parse_colour bindings that drop the alpha they parsed
findings.obligation: The word is the one thing that tells the operator a quiet control is there, so a word she cannot see must neither earn the exemption nor pass 4.5:1.
findings.observation: parse_colour returns the alpha and both bindings discard it, so a word painted rgba with alpha 0, or any translucent value, is read as opaque ink and the ratio is computed as if it were solid: such a control is exempt from the boundary rule and legible at the same time. The two halves of one reading differ, because the wordless half does test alpha below 1 before it lets a border identify a control. The pre-existing body-text readings drop the ink alpha the same way, so this is a convention the delta inherits rather than one it invents, which is why it is recorded as low and not blocking.
findings.remediation: Treat a word whose alpha is below 1 as no word, or blend it over wordBehind, before the 4.5:1 comparison.

No step is orphaned by the migration: the retired phrase 'every large-text and control-boundary pair reaches at least 3 to 1' appears in no feature file, and the three new phrases appear only at canzan-theme-system.feature lines 167-169, each matched by one new #[then] regex. The browser lane itself was not re-run: the author reports us-cts-01 8/8, ui-nav-polish 26/26, nav-quick-actions 9/9 and nav-collapse-icon-rail 17/17 at this commit, and the judgments below rest on the bytes plus this compile, not on a restamped run.

THE EXEMPTION CANNOT PASS A WORDLESS CONTROL. a_word_names_it requires inTheNav AND glyph AND a non-empty word, and the word comes from wordOf, which skips any text node that fails drawn() - clip-path other than none, display none, visibility hidden, opacity 0, or a box under 4x4 px - skips any node under aria-hidden=true, and demands an [A-Za-z0-9] character, so a glyph character is no word. The shipped glyph-only nav control proves it on the live document: button.nav-collapse holds only span.nav-collapse__glyph, aria-hidden=true, text chevron, so its word reads empty, it stays on the wordless side and is read for 3:1 - and the stylesheet gives it border 1px solid var(--cz-muted) over the opaque var(--cz-bg-2), so that reading is satisfied rather than vacuous.

THE MIGRATED ROW GOES RED ON THE WRONG IMPLEMENTATION. A nav control that drops its visible word falls to the wordless side, where the two lower controls compute 0:1 - .sidebar__item carries border 0 and background transparent, .theme-toggle carries border 0 and background var(--cz-bg-2), which is the very surface the ratio is taken against - so the 3:1 assertion fires. A quiet control whose word falls under 4.5:1 fires assert_the_word_is_legible, and that reading is anchored on the word Sign out, so it cannot measure nothing and call it a pass. Both palettes are read: the dark session by the three new steps, the light twin by then_the_same_holds_when_the_device_preference_is_light, which now calls both halves.

EARLIER FINDING F1 IS RESOLVED. then_the_nav_offers_exactly now sorts both the wanted and the found places before assert_eq, so the row reads the declared observation - the SET of word-and-href pairs - and no longer the order the document happens to write them in, which the design lists as not observed. The comparison stays a sorted Vec, so multiplicity is kept and an extra, a missing or a duplicated place still fails; the failure message was reworded from 'in that order' to 'exactly'.

EARLIER FINDING F2 IS RESOLVED. The short-page row is retitled 'On a page with nothing to scroll the whole nav fits her window' and its comment now states the measured change instead of denying it: with the open nav the rail measured 0 to 769 px in a 757 px window before, because it stretched to the height of the whole shell. The title matches the acceptance row for P3, and its RED-trigger names both wrong fixes - a rule that lifts the rail out of the shell, and a cap that puts a place outside the box. Both geometry examples are kept.

The three prepared questions - whether the anti-vacuity guard detects a widened exemption, whether a clipped word earns the exemption, and who owns the unread-geometry gap - were judged locally from the bytes instead, and that limit is retained here rather than hidden.

diagnostic: ACCEPTED, delta only. The migrated control-boundary law keys the exemption on the word the control actually draws, so it cannot pass a wordless control: wordOf rejects a clipped, hidden, zero-opacity, sub-4-px or aria-hidden text node and demands an alphanumeric character, and the shipped glyph-only button.nav-collapse reads an empty word, stays on the 3:1 side and is satisfied there by its own border over an opaque fill, so that reading is non-vacuous on the live document. The row goes red on each named wrong implementation: a control that loses its word measures 0:1 on both lower controls, and a quiet control whose word falls under 4.5:1 fires the word reading, which is anchored on Sign out so it cannot measure nothing. Both palettes are read. Earlier F1 and F2 are resolved: the offered places are now compared as the declared set, with multiplicity kept, and the short-page row states the change it measured instead of denying it. The step crate compiles clean in the VM, exit 0, and no step is orphaned by the migration. Four findings are retained, none blocking craft. One belongs to design: in the narrowed rail and at phone width both lower controls draw no word, the migrated predicate puts them on the wordless side where they measure 0:1, and the ADR does not say which rule holds when the rail draws the icon alone - no row opens that geometry, so neither the scope nor the result is observed, and the scope must be decided before a row can be written. Three belong to the oracle: the anti-vacuity guard counts any non-exempt control carrying a glyph, so it does not detect the widening risk Y8 names; the row's words promise a glyph beside the word while .sidebar__icon is display none at the width read; and the word reading drops the alpha it parsed, a convention it inherits from the body-text readings. Capability limit retained: typesafe unavailable, exit 3, the key being absent from this environment, so the three prepared questions were judged locally from the bytes. The browser lane was not re-run here and the author's green counts are not restamped as a new execution; implementation GREEN and the live geometry readings stay completion obligations.
